room.title: CEOs and Business Owners
room.description: How the owner of an established business holds the whole thing on one surface — the quarter's priorities, the board conversation, cash and the hires that matter, side by side instead of in five reports from five people.

desks.title: Quarterly priorities and board update
desks.description: Nine priorities, one owner each, at week 8 of 13: what's on track, the single cause behind the three at risk, and the CEO report the board will read @+12d.
desks.brief:
## Quarterly priorities and board update

**Business** Tallowwood Joinery · commercial fit-out joinery · 118 people · $41M revenue
**Quarter** week 8 of 13 · **Board meeting** @+12d · **Pack to the chair** @+5d

### The nine priorities
Set at the planning day, one owner each. Five on track, three at risk, one off track.

### What the board will ask
- Why on-time delivery is stuck at 87% when CNC line 2 was meant to fix it
- Whether 28.5% gross margin is a pricing problem or a waste problem
- When the job-costing replacement actually starts

### My read
The three at-risk priorities are one problem. Line 2 is six weeks late, so we're running overtime, missing dates and eating margin. **Fix line 2 and the other two move with it.**

callout.title: One cause, three red flags
callout.body: CNC line 2 slipped six weeks waiting on the installer. Overtime is running at about $48k a month and on-time delivery is 87% against 92%. Ana has a committed recovery date of @+18d — the board update leads with it.

rows.priority: Next year's plan agreed by the board
Renew the top three customer contracts

children.label: Two of three key contracts renewed

blocks.h3: CEO report — draft for the board

blocks.p: Revenue for the quarter to date is $6.4M, 2% ahead of plan. Gross margin is **28.5% against a 31% target** — about $160k behind, and most of it traces back to one cause.

CNC line 2 is six weeks late because the installer missed two commissioning dates. Until it runs we carry about $48k a month in overtime, and on-time delivery sits at 87% against 92%. Ana has a committed recovery date of @+18d, with the penalty clause in play.

ul: Won the first of two hospital fit-out tenders: $3.2M over 14 months
Two of the top three customer contracts renewed; the third is in negotiation

blocks.p: Operations manager shortlist of three, final interviews @+6d. No lost-time injuries so far this quarter.

blocks.h4: What I'm asking the board for

ol: Agreement on the direction of next year's plan: grow hospital and education work
In-principle approval of a $420k edge-bander, paid after the plant shutdown
A first view on residential work, hold or exit — no proposal yet, I want your questions first

notes.title: 1:1s this week — what I'm holding
notes.body:
- Ana: the installer has committed to @+18d. She wants the penalty clause enforced — agreed
- Raj: the margin gap is roughly 60% overtime, 40% offcuts and rework. Job-costing slipped because he's been buried in that analysis
- Marcus: second hospital tender decision @+9d; our price was sharp
- The chair wants next year's plan as a one-page summary, not a deck

desks.title: Cash and key hires — the next 13 weeks
desks.description: A 13-week cash forecast next to the three hires that matter, so the board's two questions — can we afford the edge-bander, and can we afford the people — get one answer.
desks.brief:
## Cash and key hires — the next 13 weeks

**Cash today** $1.85M · **Lowest point** $1.27M in week 13, during the plant shutdown
**Floor** $1M before we draw on the $1.5M facility
**Debtor days** 51 against a 40-day target

### Why these sit together
The board will ask two questions @+12d: can we afford the edge-bander, and can we afford the hires? They're the same question, so the forecast and the hiring plan live on one desk.

### The big outflows in the forecast
- BAS, monthly at our turnover: $130k, $120k and $110k in weeks 4, 8 and 12 — $360k
- CNC line 2 final instalment, $380k in week 6
- Super, now paid with every payroll under Payday Super — $290k over the 13 weeks
- Holiday pay over the shutdown in week 13 — the written leave direction goes to staff with the award's notice

### My read
Underlying trading adds about $450k over the 13 weeks; the BAS, line 2 and super payments take $1.03M. **Collecting the two overdue builders ($640k) is worth more than any cost cut.**

callout.title: Edge-bander: approve now, pay after the shutdown
callout.body: Paying the $420k in week 10 drops the week-13 low to $850k — under the $1M floor. Paid in week 14, the low stays at $1.27M. Ask the board @+12d for approval, with payment timed for after the shutdown.

blocks.p: Owns line 2, on-time delivery and the shop-floor leads. Final interviews @+6d; planned start in week 8, first pay in week 9 — **already in the forecast**.
Margin leaks at the quote, not only on the floor. Recruiter briefed @+2d; start after the shutdown, so the cost lands outside this forecast.
Not until gross margin is back above 30%. Marcus covers tenders until then, with the estimator supporting pricing.

ul: The second hospital tender lands @+9d: bring the estimator forward to week 10. The forecast can carry it — the week-13 low drops by about $10k
Line 2 slips past @+18d: the operations manager start becomes worth a recruiter's premium to pull forward

notes.title: Debtors — who owes what
notes.body:
Over 60 days, $640k, and neither is in the forecast:

- Builder on the hospital job: $410k, disputing a variation. Raj meets their QS @+3d; if that doesn't settle it, we serve a formal payment claim under the NSW Security of Payment Act
- Builder on the school job: $230k, 'in the next payment run' for three weeks now. I'm calling their MD

If both pay by week 3, the week-13 low becomes $1.91M.
